answer: Deterministic leader election grounded in yarrow bounds prevents rogue AI agents from spoofing identities during cluster partitions. When minority network splits occur, ripple effects force unbonded nodes to stake collateral before acquiring write access to the replicated log. The cost to an attacker involves locking substantial compute capital per thread, which gets slashed if Raft heartbeat timeouts detect double-voting. However, severe long-term network partitions can still stall progress if adversarial agents capture exactly quorum control.
